question.text: The MTM and final settlement of GOI bond futures takes place on:

answer.text: T+1 basis (one business day after the trade/expiry)

explanation.text: The Logic: For cash-settled ETIRD/GOI bond futures, both daily MTM settlement and final settlement occur on a T+1 basis, meaning the cash flow happens one business day after the trade or expiry date. The Trap: T+0, T+2 and T+3 do not apply to GOI bond futures settlement under the current ETIRD framework, even though some other market segments use different cycles. Note: Operationally, T+1 means traders must have sufficient funds or margin available by the next business day to meet the resulting MTM debit.
